title: Foreclosure Relief and Extension for Servicemembers Act of 2014
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Foreclosure Relief and Extension for Servicemembers Act of 2014 - Amends the Honoring America's Veterans and Caring for Camp Lejeune Families Act of 2012 to extend through calendar year 2015 the one-year period after a service member's military service during which: (1) a court may stay proceedings to enforce an obligation on real or personal property owned by the service member before such military service; and (2) any sale, foreclosure, or seizure of such property shall be invalid without a court order or waiver agreement signed by the service member.

Revives, effective January 1, 2016 (currently, January 1, 2015), the old nine-month period in place of the one-year period granted by such Act.

summary.headline: A 2014 law extends, through 2015, the one-year protection that keeps lenders from foreclosing on some property owned by service members before their military service.
summary.what_it_does: Under the law, a court may pause enforcement actions on a debt tied to property a service member owned before military service. A sale, foreclosure, or seizure of that property is invalid without a court order or a waiver signed by the service member. The law extends this one-year period through calendar year 2015 and brings back the older nine-month period starting January 1, 2016.

who_it_affects.group: Service members who owned property before their military service
who_it_affects.how: They can get court-ordered pauses on enforcement of debts tied to that property and cannot lose it to a sale or foreclosure without a court order or a signed waiver during the protected period.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders and loan servicers holding debts on such property
who_it_affects.how: They must get a court order or a signed waiver before selling, foreclosing on, or seizing covered property during the protected period, and courts may pause their enforcement actions.

who_it_affects.group: Courts handling enforcement cases involving service members
who_it_affects.how: They have the authority to stay proceedings to enforce obligations on covered property during the protected period.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 18, 2014. The one-year protection period applies through calendar year 2015, and the nine-month period takes effect January 1, 2016.
